role: RawRRBackup extension: the append-only streaming backup (header JSON + JSONL points, each point line sealed with EncryptionManager and base64-encoded when the key is reachable, plain JSON otherwise with the session queued in PendingEncryptionLedger; files under BackupProtection.appendable; a points file already on disk kept and appended to; a missing or set-aside points file rewritten with every point so far), point reading/merging (deduplicated by timestamp) with .corrupted_* siblings, beat-count reconciliation, backup-directory protection migration, index load/save (with a pre-write merge of an index the launch could not read, or could not set aside), BackupError, and helpers shared with WorkoutTrackBackup: BackupProtection (the protection classes), SealedJSONLines (the sealed line format and its re-seal), BackupFiles (verified removal) and JSONLinesFile (append after cutting a torn last line, also used by SystemDiagnosticsManager).
types: RawRRBackup: extension — append-format streaming backup and index I/O
BackupProtection: enum — appendable (until first unlock), appendableClass, plaintext (complete unless open)
SealedJSONLines: enum — encode/open/re-seal JSON Lines whose lines are sealed with EncryptionManager
BackupFiles: enum — remove files and report those left
JSONLinesFile: enum — append to a JSON Lines file after cutting a torn last line (shared by RawRRBackup, WorkoutTrackBackup and SystemDiagnosticsManager)

units.does: Merges an index the launch could not read (throws while it is still unreadable). When the points hold no more than the row's backedUpCount, only retries an index save a failed write left owed (saveIndexIfOwed, throws when it fails again) and returns. Otherwise appends points beyond backedUpCount to the session's JSONL file — starting the append format first (startAppendFormatIfNew) when there is no entry or a one-shot entry, refusing (wouldReplaceLargerBackup) when that one-shot holds more beats; a points file already on disk for an id with no row is kept and appended to, never truncated — then updates and saves the index with backedUpCount = points.count, and only after that removes the replaced one-shot file. Lines are sealed (encodedLines); a batch with plain lines queues the session in the raw-backup ledger before it is written. writeAppendData cuts a torn last line before appending and is handed every point too (encoded only when used): a points file that is missing, or unreadable and set aside, is written again with the whole night, so the stored count is what the file holds. Any write or set-aside failure throws before the index moves, leaving the beats buffered for the next call; an index save that throws leaves memory at the count the file holds, marked owed, so no point is appended twice. It returns only once the points and the row are both on disk. Until the switch completes the index still names the one-shot backup, which stays readable.

branches.cond: launch index read failed and file still unreadable

branches.effect: continue; else retry an owed index save (saveIndexIfOwed, rethrows) and return
startAppendFormatIfNew refuses if the one-shot holds more beats, else keeps a readable header and points file already there or writes them; returns whether it switched

branches.cond: points file appendable / missing or set aside / cannot be set aside
branches.effect: appends the new batch / writes every point fresh / throws before the index is updated

branches.cond: switched from a one-shot backup with a file name
branches.effect: removes that file, after the points and the index are written

units.does: Removes the one-shot backup file a completed format switch replaced; a failed removal is logged and leaves a file the index no longer names (a session still queued for re-encryption stays queued, and reencryptBackup removes a plaintext one).

For a session with no index entry or a one-shot entry: refuses (refuseReplacingLargerBackup) when the one-shot holds more beats than newCount, else starts the append format (startAppendFormat) and returns true. Returns false for a session already in the append format.

branches.cond: one-shot holds more beats than newCount

units.does: Throws BackupError.wouldReplaceLargerBackup when the given (one-shot) index entry's beatCount exceeds newCount; returns otherwise (including nil).

Starts the append format without destroying beats: keeps a header already on disk that decodes, else writes one (captureDate = the replaced entry's captureDate, else now) atomically with BackupProtection.appendable (writeHeaderUnlessReadable); keeps a points file already on disk that reads, else sets an unreadable one aside and starts an empty one (keepOrStartPointsFile). A one-shot backup being replaced is left on disk; appendBackup removes it once the new copy is written and indexed.

branches.effect: a new header keeps it; else now

units.does: Keeps the session's header when it exists and decodes (decodedHeader through attempt, a failure logged): it was written by a first append whose index save never happened, and its date is the real start. Otherwise writes the given header atomically with BackupProtection.appendable; throws when that write fails.

When the points file exists and reads as UTF-8 it is kept (the batch is appended after the beats it holds; a read merges both by time). When it exists but does not read, it is set aside (preserveCorruptedPointsFile; throws if that move fails, nothing written). Then, if not kept, writes an empty points file with BackupProtection.appendable.

branches.effect: readable: return, kept; unreadable: set aside (throws if it cannot be), then start empty

units.does: Reads and decodes (iso8601 dates) the BackupHeader at url; throws on a read or decode failure.

Encodes the points as JSONL via SealedJSONLines.encode with the stored manager when its key is reachable: each line sealed and base64-encoded, the rest of the batch plain JSON once sealing fails or with no key. When any line is plain, logs at .error and records the session in the raw-backup PendingEncryptionLedger before returning (so before the bytes are written). Throws only when a point does not encode.

Decodes one points-file line: SealedJSONLines.open returns a plain JSON line as it is, or base64-decodes and decrypts a sealed one (SealedJSONLines.Failure.unreadableLine when not base64); then decodes the RRPoint.

Appends the new batch through JSONLinesFile.append (read/write handle, torn last line cut off first so the batch does not fuse with it, a failed write cut back and reported); a write failure is rethrown. If no handle opens and the file exists, rewrites its complete lines plus the batch atomically (rewriteKeepingExisting); if those bytes won't read it is set aside first, and a set-aside that fails throws (BackupError.couldNotSetAside) with nothing written. Otherwise (file missing or just set aside) writes allLines() — every point so far — as a fresh file with completeFileProtectionUntilFirstUserAuthentication, logging and rethrowing on failure.

branches.effect: .appended: return; .writeFailed: rethrow its error; .couldNotOpen: fall through
return; false (set aside) → fall through to the fresh write; a failed set-aside throws

units.does: Reads the existing points file and atomically writes its complete lines (JSONLinesFile.completeLines, a torn last line dropped) plus the new bytes, returning true; if unreadable, sets it aside (preserveCorruptedPointsFile) and returns false, or throws when that move fails so nothing is written over it.

branches.effect: write combined, return true; else set aside and return false (a failed set-aside throws)

units.does: Renames the points file to <name>.corrupted_<ms> in the backup directory, the stamp raised past any name already taken so two set-asides in one moment never collide; readAllPointLines, corruptedSiblingNames and cleanupAppendFiles find it by the .corrupted_ prefix. A failed move is logged and throws BackupError.couldNotSetAside.

branches.effect: log warning; throw couldNotSetAside (file stays in place)

units.does: Replaces the session's index row with an append-format row (captureDate kept or now, archived kept, lastBackupTime now, beat counts = beatCount) and saves the index.

Reads the header and all point lines (live + corrupted siblings), throws noDataToBackup when none, checks the count against the index, and returns a BackupEntry with a hash computed over the recovered points.

Merges points from every .corrupted_ sibling and the live file keyed by t_ms (live wins, duplicates collapse) and returns them sorted by time; without siblings the live file must exist (its read throws otherwise).

branches.effect: read it; a failed read is logged and skipped (?? [])

branches.cond: no siblings, or live file exists
branches.effect: read the live file (throws if missing), overwriting by t_ms

units.does: Lists backup-directory names beginning '<points name>.corrupted_' (internal: also used by backupSize).
Reads a JSONL file as UTF-8 and decodes each line with decodePointLine (plain or sealed), skipping lines that fail and logging the skipped count once.

branches.effect: one log line with the count

units.does: When recovered differs from the index backedUpCount: lowers the stored count to recovered if fewer and the last backup is older than 600 s (or unknown); otherwise logs a mismatch warning.
Creates the backup directory if missing, sets completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication on it, and migrates existing file protection; logs failures.

Sets BackupProtection.appendableClass (completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication) on every non-hidden file in the backup directory except one-shot files (OneShotBackupName.parse) of sessions pending re-encryption, which keep their plaintext class; the header and points files of a pending session are migrated like any other. A listing failure is logged and migrates nothing; setAttributes failures are counted and logged once.

branches.cond: file is not a one-shot file of a pending raw-backup id

units.does: The session's header URL followed by appendPointFiles (points file and .corrupted_* copies).
The session's points file URL followed by the URLs of its .corrupted_* siblings (corruptedSiblingNames; a failed listing gives none).

Removes the session's header, points and .corrupted_* files (appendFiles) through BackupFiles.remove and returns those still on disk (discardable); a missing file counts as removed, other failures are logged.

Loads backup_index.json: absent → keep empty; read error → set indexReadFailed and keep in-memory index; read OK → decode, or rebuild from files when it does not decode, and store under the lock, setting indexReadFailed when the undecodable file could not be moved aside (so the next save re-reads it and is blocked until it moves).

Decodes [BackupIndex] (iso8601) and returns it with replaceable=true; on decode failure logs and returns recoverIndexFromFiles() (the rebuilt rows, replaceable=false when the file could not be moved aside).

branches.effect: log error and rebuild from files

units.does: When the launch read failed (or an undecodable index could not be moved aside): if the index file no longer exists (purged) just clears the flag; otherwise re-reads it (throws while still unreadable), throws BackupError.couldNotSetAside while it does not decode and still cannot be moved aside, and otherwise clears the flag and adds on-disk (or rebuilt) rows whose ids are not already in memory.
Under indexLock runs mergeIndexThatFailedToLoad, so a write first merges an index the launch could not read; throws while the file still cannot be read.

Under indexLock: marks the index save owed (indexSaveOwed = true), merges a previously unreadable index, encodes the index (iso8601, pretty, sorted) and writes it atomically with completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication, then clears indexSaveOwed. A merge, encode or write that throws leaves indexSaveOwed set, so saveIndexIfOwed retries it.
Reads indexSaveOwed under indexLock; when set, saves the index (saveIndex), rethrowing its error; otherwise does nothing.
English (non-localized) text for BackupError cases.
units.entry: LocalizedError witness; read via localizedDescription in logs/recovery errors

branches.effect: kept-file message naming the file that could not be read or moved aside
kept-backup message naming the files that could not be removed

units.does: The EncryptionManager from AppDependencies.current.storage when isAvailable (its key can be loaded or created), else nil.

Encodes each item with the given encoder as one newline-terminated line, sealed through sealedOrPlain while a manager is held; after the first sealing failure the rest of the batch is plain. Returns the bytes and allSealed (true when the manager survived, or nothing was encoded). Throws only when an item does not encode.

branches.effect: encode, seal or not, append newline

units.does: With no sealer returns the JSON unchanged. Otherwise returns encrypt(json) base64-encoded; when encrypt throws, logs at .error, sets sealer to nil (the rest of the batch goes plain) and returns the JSON.
The JSON a line holds: a plain line (isPlain) as it is; otherwise base64-decodes it (throws Failure.unreadableLine when it is not base64) and decrypts it with the manager.
True when the line's first byte can start a JSON value ({ [ " - 0-9 t f n); sealed lines start with 'R' (base64 of the FR framing). An empty line is not plain.
Whether any newline-separated line of the data is plain (isPlain).

The data with each plain line replaced by its sealed, base64-encoded form and every other byte unchanged (empty lines and a trailing line without its newline kept as they were). Throws when encrypt throws.

Reads the file; with no plain line returns true untouched. Otherwise writes resealed bytes atomically with BackupProtection.appendable (the class streamed files are created with), reads the file back and returns true when it holds no plain line. Throws when the read, sealing or write fails.
Removes each URL that exists (a failure is logged through attempt) and returns the URLs still on disk afterwards; a file already gone counts as removed.

Opens a read/write FileHandle on the file (forUpdating; a failure is logged by attempt and returns .couldNotOpen with nothing written), cuts off a torn last line (dropTornTail), seeks to the end noting that offset and writes the data, returning .appended. A cut or seek that throws returns .writeFailed(error); a write that throws truncates the file back to the noted offset (a failed truncate is logged) and returns .writeFailed(error). The handle is closed on every path (a failed close is logged).

branches.effect: truncate back to the start offset, return .writeFailed(error); else return .appended

units.does: Seeks to the end of the open handle; an empty file, or one whose last byte is a newline, is left as it is. Otherwise reads the last 64 KB (or the whole file when shorter) and truncates the file just after its last newline; when that window holds no newline, truncates to empty if the window was the whole file and otherwise leaves the file unchanged. Throws when a seek, read or truncate throws.

branches.effect: truncate to 0 when the window is the whole file, else leave it; return
truncate just after the last newline

units.does: Returns the bytes up to and including their last newline: all of them when empty or ending with a newline, none when they hold no newline.

branches.cond: data empty or ends with a newline
